requirements.summary: The site builds and deploys on a currently supported Next.js and Node runtime, and the production origin is observed serving that build. Measured at the researched commit: the tree cannot build on any Node version Vercel offers.

The site is rebuilt as a Next.js App Router application whose UI is partitioned into the comp's seven independent regions, so region work runs in parallel and no two tickets share a file, and each region reproduces the comp's geometry and colour channels with the measured geometry defects corrected rather than transcribed.
Every claim on the site is the authoritative resume or measured data: no placeholder copy, no invented employer, and no hardcoded figure.

The activity surface is affordable and operable: the generated payload is delivered newest-first inside a hard first-byte budget, and every control meets WCAG 2.2 AA for accessible naming that does not depend on a glyph, keyboard operation, and pause/stop/hide under reduced motion.

Every repository and contribution figure the site displays is derived from measured GitHub data at generation time, no figure is a literal in copy or code, and the visualization replays that measured history with honest lifespan semantics.

Attribution and encoding are ground-truthful and reproducible: commit authorship resolves to exactly the two actor logins through an author-email allowlist with no false positives from same-name third parties and no silent false negatives, every visual scale is anchored in design-system tokens rather than hand-tuned values, and the build and client runtime are hermetic and deterministic so CI can assert semantics before it asserts pixels.

The site is safe to publish and safe to read: no personal contact data reaches the repository or the build output, and wherever colour carries meaning the encoding is paired with a non-colour channel that survives greyscale and common colour-vision deficiencies.

The system is a deterministic function of its inputs — the same inputs produce byte-identical output on every run — and the site's copy is real indexable text generated from the single content/ source rather than from pixels.

The page carries a correct heading outline, landmark structure, bypass affordance and keyboard/pointer parity, including a real text equivalent for every canvas surface, and the resume surfaces render with zero client JavaScript.

Every pull request is gated by a hermetic browser-level proof, built by this repository and exercised in a version-pinned browser container with zero dependency on any hosted preview deployment, and the interactive instrument stays inside its measured frame budget.
The activity system degrades safely: a transient upstream failure never loses history, and a partial or empty upstream response is refused rather than published.

decisions.summary: One foundation ticket lands the toolchain and the CI gate atomically.
decisions.rationale: C-4 shows Next and Tailwind/PostCSS must move as a unit or the build is red, and C-14 shows deleting yarn.lock without regenerating package-lock.json is red. Any split leaves the repository red, violating the ticket boundary rule. The Executor's mandatory 'fresh CI green on the exact pull-request head' cannot be satisfied until a workflow exists, so CI cannot be deferred. Rejected: three sequential foundation tickets, which add two waves of serialization before any parallel work; and splitting CI out, which leaves wave 2 ungated.

decisions.summary: Next 16.2.12 + React 19.2.8 + Tailwind 4.3.3 + TypeScript 5.9.3 + ESLint 9.39.5 on the App Router, with no output:'export'.
decisions.rationale: The toolchain must move as a unit anyway (C-4). The App Router is chosen for React Server Component zero-JS resume panes, which answers the content track's zero-indexable-text finding. Static export is rejected on headers for JSON cache-control and remote-avatar optimization, not on the apex-to-www redirect, which the Next.js verifier showed export would not regress. Rejected: incremental 10-to-11-to-16 hops; the Pages Router; static export.

decisions.summary: package.json and package-lock.json are frozen after the foundation ticket, which pre-installs the entire measured dependency set and pre-declares every npm script.
decisions.rationale: About seven downstream tickets would otherwise all edit both files, forcing serializes_with edges across the two widest waves and collapsing parallelism. This is the highest-leverage single move in the plan, and it matters more because aiur materializes each agent workspace copy-on-write from a prewarm base that has already run npm ci. Rejected: per-ticket dependency installs, which cause a lockfile conflict storm; a dependencies ticket per wave, which serializes anyway.

decisions.summary: All control glyphs become inline SVG icon components.
decisions.rationale: C-28 records that two research tracks independently found the media-control and Braille codepoints outside JetBrains Mono's coverage. Inline SVG is also required for accessible names, and it removes DesignSync from the critical path. Rejected: subsetting twelve woff2 files; a Nerd Font patched build, on licence and weight grounds; accepting fallback-font rendering, which produces tofu on machines whose fallback stack lacks the codepoints.

decisions.summary: Zero serializes_with pairs. Every same-wave ticket owns a disjoint write surface: one module per region, one shell that mounts them.
decisions.rationale: C-11 measured that serializes_with is the one edge type aiur does not enforce at runtime, so relying on it is both unsafe and slow. Partitioning by file removes the need for it entirely. Rejected: sweep tickets such as a single accessibility pass or a single mobile pass that touch every region file.

decisions.summary: The data pipeline splits by authentication surface: the clone half is anonymous and tokenless, the GraphQL half uses an SSO-authorized PAT.
decisions.rationale: GT-1, GT-2 and GT-3 measured that SAML blinds the API but not git. Two different secrets, two different failure modes and two different review boundaries follow, and the split makes the human gate narrow because only the grid half blocks. Rejected: a single pipeline on GITHUB_TOKEN, which measurably produces wrong numbers; scraping the anonymous HTML, whose markup changed during the research session.

decisions.summary: Scheme D encoding: 1,500-event chunks, one global front-coded path dictionary sliced 1:1, newest-first numbering, a 12 KB gzip dictionary-slice split guard and a 12 KB brotli CI first-byte budget.
decisions.rationale: The data-pipeline track measured 12.9x better first byte than year-chunking because 76.2% of events fall in 2026. The split guard was raised from 8,192 B because the verifier measured a true maximum of 8,250 B, which fires the original guard. Rejected: year chunks, at a 103 KB first chunk; repository chunks, at 88 KB for aiur alone; self-contained per-chunk dictionaries, at 1.4-1.5x total inflation.

decisions.summary: No contribution figure is a literal anywhere in copy. Every number reads from the payload, which carries generatedAt, windowStart, windowEnd, dayCount and repoCountDefinition.
decisions.rationale: This retires C-1 and C-20 permanently and prevents the comp's three-inconsistent-windows defect from recurring. Rejected: pinning 1,826 days; pinning 2,038 days. Both are wrong under SAML and both go stale daily.

decisions.summary: A gruvbox-anchored 10-stop contribution ramp (#3c3836 #404a2b #4d5b21 #5e6a1f #70791d #83881b #98971a #b8bb26 #d9d34a #faeb77), one single ramp for the grid with combined actors, and a CIEDE2000 fixture in CI.
decisions.rationale: GT-17 measured that the ramp hits --green-d and --green exactly, so design-token changes propagate rather than drift. GT-15 measured that the contrast argument between the candidates is a wash. Rejected: the comp's synthetic OKLCh sweep, which hits no token and clips agent levels 7 through 9.

decisions.summary: Lifespan-interval visibility with dimmed ghost outlines for dead repositories, recorded explicitly as a product decision.
decisions.rationale: This honours the viz-runtime verifier's [unproven] marking rather than overstating it. Ghosts preserve the ground-truth 'longer stay means more history' property without the dishonesty of monotonic accumulation. Rejected: monotonic accumulation, under which 2021 shows repositories that did not exist yet; lifespan with hard removal, which reads as arbitrary vanishing.

decisions.summary: Canvas for the interactive grid plus a visually-hidden <table> as the text alternative, with a <noscript> fallback that doubles as the SEO surface.
decisions.rationale: This resolves C-26 and the Next.js track's SVG proposal simultaneously. The table is also the only viable answer to WCAG 1.4.11 being unsatisfiable at this density (GT-15) and to axe-core being structurally blind to canvas content. Rejected: an interactive DOM/SVG grid, at 1,827 event targets and with no shadowBlur; canvas alone, which has zero indexable text and zero accessibility.

decisions.summary: Auto-merge on, no merge queue, required_approving_review_count 0, CODEOWNERS scoped to gate files only, and strict_required_status_checks_policy false.
decisions.rationale: C-21 and C-11 together. A merge queue is structurally unavailable on a User-owned repository (GT-11: owner_type User, plan null). Strict up-to-date checks make agents thrash on rebases with no queue to absorb the churn. Rejected: human-gated merges, which cap throughput; a merge queue, which does not exist for this account type.

decisions.summary: Issues are created only by publish_build_order.py.
decisions.rationale: C-11 measured that depends_on is enforced at runtime only as GitHub-native issue dependencies written by the publisher. gh issue create silently discards the graph, so hand-created issues would produce an unordered fleet. Rejected: hand-created issues.

decisions.summary: Keep an honest 'fresh - Nh ago' pill driven by generatedAt, and delete emitLive()'s random re-roll and its 2600 ms interval.
decisions.rationale: The live-transport scope cut removes the transport, not the freshness signal. emitLive is a local synthesiser in the design prototype, and a synthesised 'live' event is a lie that this site's target audience will spot. Rejected: removing the pill entirely, which loses the dashboard affordance; keeping emitLive, which fabricates data.

decisions.summary: The phone number <redacted-personal-phone> never enters the repository or the build output. The email decision is deferred to GATE-005.
decisions.rationale: The content track's SIM-swap analysis, confirmed by its verifier. kevinweaver.dev already has five live Namecheap MX records, so an alias is a registrar-panel row rather than a new service. Rejected: obfuscation, which does not survive OCR; publishing the number as-is.

decisions.summary: mulberry32 for the seeded RNG, carried as a 32-bit integer field on SimState and advanced functionally inside step.
decisions.rationale: C-24 records that mulberry32 uses only Math.imul and >>>, so it is bit-identical across V8 versions and architectures. The integer-field form fixes both the purity violation and the structuredClone throw that a closure-based generator causes. Rejected: xorshift128, the viz-runtime proposal, which states no cross-engine guarantee; a closure-based RNG, which throws under structuredClone.

decisions.summary: Scheduled regeneration runs on GitHub Actions, never Vercel Cron. The workflow always commits, at minimum a generatedAt bump, and declares workflow_dispatch.
decisions.rationale: C-29's surviving grounds. Public repositories auto-disable scheduled workflows after 60 days of no activity, and this repository has had zero pushes since 2021-05-31, so it is already the failure case. Rejected: Vercel Cron; Vercel Blob or Global Config, at a 1 MB cap and 100 writes per month on Hobby.

tickets.title: Foundation: toolchain re-scaffold and green CI gate
tickets.outcome: On a clean clone of the merged branch, `npm ci && npm run typegen && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build` exits 0 on Node 24, `next build` prerenders a blank-but-Tailwind-styled App Router page, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` publishes a single `ci-ok` status context on every pull request — green even when every expensive job is skipped.
scope: Replace the Next 10.1.3 / React 17 / Tailwind 2 / ESLint 7 toolchain with the measured pin set in one atomic change, and rename `package.json` `name` from `with-tailwindcss` to `kevinweaver-dev`.
Delete `yarn.lock` and regenerate `package-lock.json` (lockfileVersion 3) from the corrected `package.json` in the same commit, leaving exactly one lockfile.
Pre-install the entire measured downstream dependency set and pre-declare every npm script, freezing `package.json` and `package-lock.json` for the remainder of the build order.
Scaffold a minimal App Router root — `app/layout.tsx`, `app/page.tsx`, `app/globals.css` containing only `@import "tailwindcss";` — that prerenders a blank-but-styled page.
Delete the dead Pages Router surface and the v2-era config files it depends on.
Add `scripts/ci/assert-pins.mjs`, a dependency-free Node script that fails the build on toolchain drift, and run it before `eslint` in CI.
Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with a `changes` job, `if:`-skipped expensive jobs, and one always-running `ci-ok` aggregator that is the sole required status context.
Add `vercel.json` with `framework`, `installCommand`, and cache-control headers for `/data/v1/*`, plus `engines.node: "24.x"` in `package.json`.
non_goals: No design-system CSS, no gruvbox tokens, no `@theme inline` bridge, no accessibility layer — KW-003 owns the contents of `app/globals.css` and all of `styles/**` from wave 2 onward.
No fonts and no icon components — KW-004 owns `public/fonts/**`, `app/fonts.ts` and `components/icons/**`.
No region components, no `app/regions/**`, no `components/ds/**`, and no real page composition — KW-005 owns the shell contract and the seven stubs.
No content strings, no resume data, no `content/**` — KW-006.

No repository governance: no labels, no rulesets, no `CODEOWNERS`, no `AGENTS.md`, no auto-merge or workflow-permission API calls — KW-002 owns all of it and deliberately does not touch `.github/workflows/**`.
No `vitest.config.mts`, no `playwright.config.ts`, no `.size-limit.json`, no `scripts/ci/check-first-load.mjs`, no `e2e/**`, no `test/**` — KW-011, KW-023, KW-030, KW-031.
No `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`, `data-bundle.yml` or `snapshots.yml` — KW-023, KW-028, KW-031.
No `NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider`, no `packageManager` field, no `output: 'export'`, and no incremental Next version hops.

C-4 proves Next and Tailwind/PostCSS must move as one change; C-14 proves the `yarn.lock` deletion and the `package-lock.json` regeneration must land in the same commit; and the fleet cannot merge anything until a CI gate exists. Every proposed subdivision leaves `main` red.
tickets.risk: high — this is the only ticket that can break the production deployment, it is the sole bootstrap of the CI gate, and its `package-lock.json` is copied into every agent workspace by aiur prewarm.

tickets.title: Repo governance: agent labels, CODEOWNERS, AGENTS.md, and auto-merge
tickets.outcome: `its-everdred/kevinweaver-dev` carries the complete label inventory that both the aiur orchestrator and the Build Order publisher require, `main` is protected by an active ruleset whose single required status check is `ci-ok`, squash-only auto-merge with branch deletion is on, the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only and cannot approve pull requests, `.github/CODEOWNERS` guards the gate files only, and root `AGENTS.md` states the agent contract in writing.
scope: Create and reconcile, idempotently, the complete GitHub label inventory: the 10 aiur lifecycle states, the 3 aiur marker labels, `model:claude`, `complexity:1`..`complexity:5`, and every Build Order projection label (`build-order`, `phase:1`..`phase:7`, and one `build-lane:<id>` per declared workstream).
Flip repository merge settings to squash-only auto-merge with automatic branch deletion.
Reduce the default Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` to `read` and disable Actions self-approval of pull requests.
Commit `.github/rulesets/main.json` and apply it, protecting `main` with exactly one required status check, `ci-ok`.
Add `.github/CODEOWNERS` covering the gate files only, so a PR that weakens a gate needs the owner's review while ordinary product PRs self-merge.
Add root `AGENTS.md` stating the build contract, the branch/PR conventions, the one-lockfile rule and the issue-creation rule.
Add `.github/pull_request_template.md` adapted from the aiur repository's template.
non_goals: Creating or editing any file under `.github/workflows/**`. KW-001 owns `ci.yml`; KW-023 owns `e2e.yml`; KW-028 owns the data workflow; KW-031 owns `snapshots.yml`. Touching them would also hit GATE-002 at push time.
Adding `e2e-ok`, a Vercel deployment status, or any second required status check to the ruleset.
Any change to `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `tsconfig.json`, or any toolchain file. KW-001 owns those and DEC-003 freezes them.
Minting, rotating or storing repository secrets. `CONTRIB_TOKEN` is GATE-003; `AUTOMERGE_TOKEN` and `SNAPSHOT_PUSH_TOKEN` belong to the workflow tickets that need them.
Creating, editing or labelling GitHub issues. DEC-013 makes `publish_build_order.py` the only issue author.
Transferring the repository to an organization or enabling a merge queue.
Adding `.env` to `.gitignore` or any other repository-hygiene change outside the four files listed under Surfaces.
tickets.complexity_rationale: One JSON config file plus three short prose documents and a fixed list of idempotent `gh` calls; no application code, no build surface, and every step is independently re-runnable.
tickets.risk: Medium despite complexity 1. The ruleset and the Actions-token change are live repository mutations that can deadlock every subsequent agent PR if the required status context is wrong or code-owner review is scoped too broadly. Every mutation below has a stated one-command rollback.

agent_gate: `gh label list --repo its-everdred/kevinweaver-dev --limit 200` lists all ten `agent:` lifecycle labels (including both `agent:cancelled` and `agent:canceled`), all three `agent:` markers, `model:claude`, `complexity:1`..`complexity:5`, `build-order`, `phase:1`..`phase:7`, and one `build-lane:<id>` label for every workstream declared in `docs/build-orders/site-rewrite/build-order.json`.
`gh api repos/its-everdred/kevinweaver-dev --jq '[.allow_auto_merge,.delete_branch_on_merge,.allow_squash_merge,.allow_merge_commit,.allow_rebase_merge]'` returns `[true,true,true,false,false]`.
`gh api repos/its-everdred/kevinweaver-dev/actions/permissions/workflow` returns exactly `{"default_workflow_permissions":"read","can_approve_pull_request_reviews":false}`.

`gh api repos/its-everdred/kevinweaver-dev/rulesets --jq 'length'` is at least 1, and the read-back of the `main` ruleset matches the worked fixture in the implementation notes: `enforcement` `active`, exactly one required status check `ci-ok`, `required_approving_review_count` 0, `require_code_owner_review` true, `strict_required_status_checks_policy` false, `allowed_merge_methods` `["squash"]`.
`jq -e . .github/rulesets/main.json` parses, and the committed file matches what was actually applied (relevant only if the `bypass_actors` fallback fired).

`git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` lists exactly `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `.github/rulesets/main.json`, `AGENTS.md` and nothing else — in particular nothing under `.github/workflows/`, and neither `package.json` nor `package-lock.json`.

`AGENTS.md` contains the literal string `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build`, forbids `yarn`, forbids `gh issue create`, and names `git branch --show-current` as the only way to read the branch.
`grep -rn "merge_group" .github/` returns nothing (C-21: merge queue is unavailable on this repo and dead config misleads agents).
at_merge_gate: This PR is squashed into `main` on verified-local-green evidence rather than on a `ci-ok` status, per GATE-006: no workflow exists on `main` while wave 1 is in flight. Every subsequent ticket requires the real `ci-ok` status.
A scratch PR opened against current `main` accepts `gh pr merge --squash --auto`, proving `allow_auto_merge` took effect; the scratch PR is then closed and its branch deleted.

A scratch PR that touches a CODEOWNERS-covered path (for example `.github/CODEOWNERS` itself) is observed to be blocked pending code-owner review, while a scratch PR touching only `README.md` is not — proving the CODEOWNERS scope is narrow rather than repository-wide. Record both observations in the PR body; if a gate-file PR authored by the code owner cannot be unblocked (GitHub does not allow a PR author to satisfy their own code-owner review), record it and escalate to the Executor before merging any workflow-touching ticket.
